name: Cucumber
grown_as: A tender annual climber, in the UK usually grown in a greenhouse up a string or cane (smooth long all-female varieties), or outdoors as a shorter, bumpy 'ridge' cucumber. William's variety is not known: drawn as a greenhouse cucumber trained up a support. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A climbing or scrambling vine 2 to 3 m, its stems four- or five-angled and roughly hairy, climbing by simple (unbranched) coiling tendrils, one at each leaf joint. In a greenhouse it is trained up one string as a single tall stem with short side shoots.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, one at each joint, with a tendril beside it
leaf.outline: Broadly triangular to heart-shaped, 10 to 20 cm, with 3 to 5 shallow, angular, pointed lobes; the end lobe is the largest and pointed
leaf.veins: Palmate, three to five main veins from the stalk top
leaf.surface: Rough, with stiff short bristles on both sides, sandpapery

flower.form: A small open yellow star or shallow bell
flower.petals: Five, joined only at the very base, oval with pointed tips, a little wrinkled, spreading
flower.centre: Male: three short stamens, yellow, close together. Female: a short three-lobed stigma.
flower.behind: Five narrow pointed green sepals. The female flower sits on top of a tiny prickly cucumber.
flower.carried: In the leaf joins: males in small clusters on short stalks, females singly; all-female greenhouse varieties have only females

fruit: Greenhouse types: long (25 to 40 cm), slim, straight cylinder, dark green, smooth and glossy, hanging from the leaf joints. Ridge types: 10 to 20 cm, stouter, paler, covered in small bumps with soft spines. Left too long they turn yellow. Seeds narrow, flat, cream-white, pointed oval, 8 to 10 mm.
seedling: Two smooth, oblong to oval seed leaves 3 to 4 cm with rounded tips; the first true leaf small, rough and angular-lobed.
winter: Nothing: killed by cold and cleared

leaf: a triangular heart-shaped leaf with 3 to 5 shallow angular pointed lobes
bloom: small yellow star of five petals joined only at the base
for a female, a tiny prickly cucumber behind the flower
seedling: a small rough angular true leaf
young: a young vine with a few angular heart-shaped leaves
a simple unbranched tendril coiling round a support
flower: a tall vine up a support with simple coiling tendrils
small yellow flowers at the leaf joints
crop: long slim dark green cucumbers hanging from the leaf joints

look_alikes: Melon leaves are rounder with blunt shallow lobes and are softer. Courgette leaves and flowers are far larger. Wild white bryony (Bryonia dioica) has deeply cut ivy-like leaves, small greenish-white flowers and red berries.
